title: Semi-Log Linearization of Exponential Decay
originalTopic: Function Modeling: Exponential Growth and Decay
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Demonstrate how the exponential model y = A*e^(k*x) is linearized on a semi-log plot, and express the growth constant k and initial amount A in terms of the linear regression parameters.
finalAnswer: \ln y = kx + \ln A; \quad \text{Slope } m = k, \quad y\text{-intercept } B = \ln A \implies A = e^B

steps.title: Apply Natural Logarithms
steps.explanation: Take natural logs of both sides and apply the logarithmic product rule.
steps.why: Natural logarithms uncouple multiplicative exponential factors.

steps.title: Simplify Using Inverse Properties
steps.explanation: Because ln and the exponential base e are mutual inverses, ln(e^(kx)) = kx.
steps.why: Inverse identity ln(e^u) = u for all real u.

steps.title: Identify Semi-Log Coordinate Linearity
steps.mathExpression: Y = m x + B \quad \text{where } Y = \ln y, \ m = k, \ B = \ln A
steps.explanation: Plotting ln y versus untransformed x yields a straight line with slope equal to the exponential growth/decay constant k and vertical intercept ln A.
steps.why: Semi-log transformations linearize exponential models directly against linear time or space.
